newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 6.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - During the currency crisis, banks profitted most by selling western currency to clients. While commercial banks charged four times the usual amount for changing money, revenue from currency exchange failed to cover losses suffered on loans.
- Gas consumption continues to rise dynamically, with 5.138 billion cubic meters being sold during the first six months of the year. This represents an 8.05 percent year on year increase.
- The pan-European ERMES pageing system should begin at least partial operation in the Czech Republic by the end of 1997.

- Insurer IPB Pojistovna announced profits approaching 17 million crowns for the first half of 1997. This represents a year-on-year decline from 36 million crowns. Company officials attribute the decline to increases in insurance payouts.

- Results indicate that after four years on the market, construction savings banks will play a decisive role in helping to solve the housing shortage. The Ceskomoravska Stavebni Sporitelna (CMSS), a market leader, announced a first half profit of 436 million crowns. For 1996, CMSS recorded a 375 million crown profit.
- The cost of repairing roads damaged by flooding has been roughly estimated at 3.5 billion crowns. Repairs of the damaged road network is expected to last through into 1998.

- ZDB Bohumin and Spolchemie Usti nad Labem issued shares for a joint holding company EPAS. The new holding company is expected to have basic capital of 1.6 billion crowns. The two founding companies should each have a share of 800 crowns in EPAS.

-The Industry and Trade Ministry is calling for loan guarantees and lower interest rates on loans to businesses affected by flooding. Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl is expected to submit the proposals to the government during the next cabinet meeting.
- Government revenues this year will not cover expenditures that have been cut twice. The government submitted to parliament a proposal to increase consumer tax.
- The Finance Ministry announced yesterday that investors have purchased 431.6 million crowns worth of flood bonds within three days of issuing the first one billion crown tranche.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Jihomaravska Energetika will buy flood bonds, despite receiving a 20 million crown, interest-free loan from the government. The energy company was one of the first five such firms to reveive the special loans from the government to help compensate for flood damage.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Kuhnl has given top priority to energy companies, as far as supplying funding for repairing flood damage. So far the government has allocated 265 million crowns to repairing damage to energy companies.

PRAVO - Officials at Cypres-based Forminster have denied any connection to KHB, Firex, IFM, IFM Melodia or Trend investment fund. Forminster, which has a majority stake in the Kotva department store, is being accused of having ties to the various investment funds by minority sharholders who tookover control of Kotva following a commercial court ruling on Monday.
